package_info.package_versions: All versions (open-source, actively used in campaigns)
package_info.why_malicious: Rafel RAT is a remote administration tool designed for Android that enables full device compromise, including data exfiltration, surveillance, and ransomware deployment. It is actively used in espionage and cybercrime campaigns, providing attackers with unauthorized access and control over victim devices.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation, upon app launch or background service start)
execution_context.file_location: Android app main activity or background service (e.g., MainActivity.java, Service.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive device information and contacts, then exfiltrates this data to a remote command-and-control server via HTTP(S), enabling espionage and privacy violation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating sensitive user data without consent is a hallmark of spyware and RATs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Android apps do not silently collect and transmit user contacts and device information to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise device management apps may collect device info, but with user consent and clear privacy policies.
key_indicators: Use of network APIs to contact external C2 servers
Access to sensitive permissions (contacts, device info)

execution_context.file_location: Android service or broadcast receiver (e.g., CommandReceiver.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a command from the C2 server, the code activates the device camera to take a photo and sends the image data to the attacker, enabling covert surveillance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remotely activating the camera without user interaction is a clear privacy violation and a common RAT tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require explicit user action to use the camera and do not send images to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Video conferencing apps use the camera, but only with user consent and visible UI.

execution_context.file_location: Android service or broadcast receiver (e.g., CommandReceiver.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a C2 command, the code sends arbitrary SMS messages from the victim device, enabling fraud, phishing, or further malware propagation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending SMS on remote command can be used for fraud, premium SMS abuse, or spreading malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not send SMS without user action or clear notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Messaging apps send SMS, but only with user intent.
key_indicators: Potential for financial or reputational harm

execution_context.file_location: Android service or broadcast receiver (e.g., CommandReceiver.java)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a C2 command, the code encrypts files on the device and notifies the attacker, enabling ransomware operations.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypting user files on remote command is a core ransomware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps do not encrypt user files without explicit user request and clear purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup apps may encrypt files, but with user consent and local storage.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the trojanized Android app (Rafel RAT) on their device.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial execution and background service start

attack_chain.action: On first run, the malware collects device info and contacts, then exfiltrates them to the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains intelligence on the victim

attack_chain.action: The malware maintains persistence and awaits commands from the C2 server.
Upon receiving commands, the malware can activate the camera for surveillance, send SMS, or encrypt files.

behavioral_signatures: Android app requesting excessive permissions (contacts, SMS, camera, microphone, location, etc.)
Background exfiltration of contacts, device info, or media files
Silent activation of camera or microphone
file_indicators: APK files with suspicious or generic names
Presence of hardcoded C2 URLs or IPs in app resources
Unusual use of Android services or broadcast receivers for remote command execution
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Rafel RAT C2 domains or IPs
Frequent HTTP(S) POST requests containing device data or media
Unusual traffic patterns from Android devices to untrusted servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Android apps for excessive permission requests and background network activity, especially exfiltration of contacts, device info, or media. Detect remote command execution by analyzing app behavior for silent camera/microphone activation, unsolicited SMS sending, or file encryption. Use network monitoring to identify connections to known C2 infrastructure and inspect outbound traffic for sensitive data leaks.
